clue.text: Performer's firm with show's host, after one's interrupted

parts.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: the host is broken into by the numeral, so one piece goes inside the other here

parts.note: an MC, master of ceremonies, hosts a show
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A stand-up's business partner, plus the show's compère, comes on after the act is cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' only orders the pieces: the firm comes first, then the host with I set inside it by 'interrupted'.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian is a kind of performer, and comic is the everyday short name for one.

clue.text: Study a branch of knowledge that intimidates all?

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
a science is an organised branch of knowledge

explanation.surface: A field of learning so fearsome it daunts everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition echoes Hamlet: 'Thus conscience does make cowards of us all'; the question mark flags the literary allusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's line says the inner moral sense makes cowards of everyone, so it cows all of us.

clue.text: Protection against water as river's rising

indicators.note: in a down clue the river's name climbs, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A flood barrier is needed because the river is rising.
explanation.walkthrough: MAC is short for mackintosh, a British raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac is a raincoat, which keeps the rain off its wearer.

clue.text: Political group, Conservative and Unionist, in endless crusade

indicators.note: the two party letters sit inside the shortened campaign word
the campaign word loses its final letter

parts.note: a cause is a campaign or crusade

explanation.surface: The Tories and Unionists join forces in a never-ending political campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative and Unionist' suggests the party itself, but the two words just supply single letters; 'endless' and 'in' do the work on the crusade word.
explanation.definitionFit: A caucus is a meeting or faction of a party's members, a political grouping.

clue.text: Blue suit Richard initially rejected

parts.note: hearts is one of the four card suits

indicators.note: the opening letter of the name is thrown out

parts.note: Dick is a pet form of Richard

explanation.surface: A depressed card player's hand, or a sad tale of Richard being turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means sad, and heartsick means sorrowful or despondent.

clue.text: Greeting applause without the least bit of surprise

indicators.note: here 'without' means outside, so the applause word encloses the letter

parts.note: a handclap is a burst of applause

indicators.note: the smallest part of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A welcome that is all applause and no surprise at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but in the old sense of outside it puts S into HANDCLAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A clasp of hands is a form of salutation when people meet.

clue.text: The woman psychologist?

definitions.meaning: Irene ... is the woman Sherlock Holmes always called 'the woman'
Alfred ... was the Austrian psychologist who founded individual psychology

explanation.walkthrough: The italic 'The' signals Holmes's phrase for Irene in Conan Doyle's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are surnames: Irene from the Holmes tales and Alfred the Viennese psychologist.

clue.text: Plant established only after revolution

indicators.note: the word for only is placed after the word for revolution

parts.note: a turn is one revolution
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: A plant takes root only once the revolution has happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'established' merely links the plant to its wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnsole is a name for heliotrope and other flowers said to turn with the sun.

clue.text: Opening moves I invite, as it might be

indicators.note: these words could be rearranged into something else, signalling the jumble

explanation.surface: Someone welcomes the first steps of a negotiation.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of I, INVITE, AS and IT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Initiatives are first steps taken to start something off.

clue.text: Ruler has the power to be heard

indicators.note: the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: if you can, you have the power or ability

explanation.surface: A sovereign holds the authority to make himself heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A khan is a ruler in Central Asia, as with Genghis Khan.

clue.text: Number curtailed visit after receiving a fright in the night

indicators.note: the visit part comes after the number
the shortened visit word takes the fright word inside it
the visit word loses its tail letter

parts.note: a call is a visit
a turn is a sudden shock, as in 'gave me a turn'

explanation.surface: A brief call that takes a scary turn after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the night' is the definition at the end; 'a fright' as a turn is a British idiom ('it gave me quite a turn'). 'curtailed', 'receiving' and 'after' handle the assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal describes things happening by night rather than by day.

clue.text: Dish from Agra I taste?

indicators.note: the dish is taken out of the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Sampling a dish from the Indian city of Agra.
explanation.walkthrough: Agra is in India, home of the Taj Mahal, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian yoghurt side dish with cucumber or mint.

clue.text: College festival

definitions.meaning: A college at both Oxford and Cambridge
A Christian feast celebrating the Eucharist

explanation.definitionFit: The name, Latin for 'body of Christ', names both Oxbridge colleges and a church feast.

clue.text: Poor children to scold, since snatching cake

parts.note: to rag is to tease or scold

indicators.note: the word for since grabs the cake and holds it inside

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it rained'
a muffin is a small cake

explanation.surface: Telling off hungry street kids for grabbing a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragamuffins are ragged, dirty children of the street.

clue.text: One who observes the old wisdom, in unusual sense

indicators.note: these letters go inside the rearranged sense
an unusual form of the word is a rearrangement of its letters

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of 'the', as in Ye Olde Shoppe
wit is good sense or wisdom

explanation.surface: An observant person applies ancient wisdom with unusual perception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns SENSE into ENESS, and 'in' sets YEWIT inside it after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness who saw an event watched it happen with their own eyes.

clue.text: Wife barred from golf-club? That's the limit

indicators.note: the wife's letter is shut out of the club

parts.note: a wedge is a lofted golf club

explanation.surface: Women not admitted to the golf club: that's going too far!
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jokes about clubs that bar women; the golf-club is the club played with.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a boundary, the furthest limit of something.

clue.text: Swan upping?

parts.note: the Swan of Avon is Shakespeare, so raising him up suggests worship of him

explanation.walkthrough: Swan upping is the British yearly census of Thames swans; here Swan is Shakespeare, the Swan of Avon, and upping means exalting him.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive adoration of Shakespeare raises the poet to a godlike height.

clue.text: Disagreeable type disturbed residents

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Unsettled local people include one awkward individual.
explanation.definitionFit: One who dissents disagrees with the majority view.

clue.text: Way man pens note in more forceful terms

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: the man encloses the note as a pen holds animals

parts.note: Roger is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man in the street writes his message more strongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... terms' is link padding round the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with more force is mightier and more powerful.

clue.text: Happen to embark on a mountain journey?

definitions.text: to embark on a mountain journey?
definitions.meaning: to reach a mountain pass, coming to it on a trek

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to occur, and literally to arrive at a route through the mountains.

clue.text: A very old wicket, so declare

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket captain declares after an ancient wicket falls.
explanation.walkthrough: To declare in cricket is to close an innings voluntarily, a misleading sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to state openly or affirm.

clue.text: Annoyed, being soaked in water, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a fire is extinguished by dousing it

explanation.definitionFit: Being irritated is one sense, and a fire doused is extinguished.

clue.text: Since beginning, describing unfashionable people's contribution?

definitions.meaning: something coming from the uncool crowd, the out set

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means from the start, and jokingly what comes from the group not in fashion.

clue.text: Sycophant now slightly changed?

indicators.note: the word's letters are altered a little into a new order

parts.note: today means now, at the present time

explanation.surface: A bootlicker who has altered his ways a little lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly changed' rearranges TODAY, a word for 'now', not the clue's word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady flatters the powerful for favour.

clue.text: Boss curtailed investigation

indicators.note: the word for investigation loses its final letter

parts.note: a study is an investigation or examination

explanation.surface: The manager cut short the inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: Boss here is a knob or raised ornament, not a manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a projecting knob, as is a decorative boss on a shield.

clue.text: Article that's fine and good

parts.note: thin means fine, as in a fine thread

explanation.surface: An object that is excellent and of quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a/the in grammar but here means an object.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is an item or object.

clue.text: Navigation instrument sending a flashing light round US city

indicators.note: the flashing light goes round the city

parts.note: a strobe is a light that flashes rapidly
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Navigators use a blinking beacon around Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrolabe measured the altitude of stars to fix position at sea.

clue.text: First to leave some craft

indicators.note: the initial letter departs from the word

parts.note: part means some, as in part of the cake

explanation.surface: The leading vessel sets off from a small fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like boats in the surface but means skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Art and craft both mean skill in making things.

clue.text: Ship from ancient city found in straggling reeds

indicators.note: the city sits inside the scrambled letters
the reeds are spread untidily, scattering their letters

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of the Iliad

explanation.surface: A vessel from Troy is discovered among the reeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straggling' describes the reeds in the surface but signals their letters are scattered; 'found in' places the city among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A destroyer is a fast warship.

clue.text: Emperor who was sent advice by Paul?

definitions.meaning: A Roman emperor, son of Vespasian

definitions.text: who was sent advice by Paul?
definitions.meaning: the New Testament has Paul's Epistle to ... giving pastoral advice

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a Roman emperor and to Paul's companion who received his letter.
